    Interactive Apps 3D Kinematics & Rotations

    3D Euler Angles, Rotation Sequences & Gimbal Lock Visualizer

    Interactive 3D laboratory for exploring all 6 Proper Euler and 6 Tait-Bryan (Roll-Pitch-Yaw) rotation sequences, intrinsic and extrinsic equivalence, symbolic & numerical 3×3 rotation matrices, dual atan2 solutions, and Gimbal Lock singularities.

    1. Select Rotation Sequence (6 Proper Euler + 6 Tait-Bryan)

    Angle triplet: (ϕ, θ, ψ)  |  Matrix product: R = R_z(ϕ) · R_y(θ) · R_z(ψ)
    Proper (Classic) Euler Sequences (6) 1st & 3rd axes identical (a₁ = a₃); singular at θ = 0°, 180°
    Tait-Bryan (Roll-Pitch-Yaw / Cardan) Sequences (6) All 3 axes distinct (a₁ ≠ a₂ ≠ a₃); singular at θ = ±90°
    Intrinsic (Current / Body-Attached Frame) Z(ϕ) → Y'(θ) → Z''(ψ) Post-multiply: 1st rotate by ϕ about ẑ, then θ about current ŷ', then ψ about current ẑ''.
    ≡
    Equivalent Extrinsic (Fixed / World Frame) Fixed Z(ψ) → Y(θ) → Z(ϕ) Reversing the rotation order and switching to the fixed frame simultaneously produces the exact same matrix R!

    Mouse Mode:
    Z-Y-Z: R = R_z(ϕ) · R_y(θ) · R_z(ψ)

    3. Gimbal Lock & Singularity Analysis

    Degrees of Freedom & Gimbal Alignment: |sin(θ)| = 0.819 (81.9%)
    Angle Between 1st Axis (ê₁) & 3rd Axis (ê₃''): ∠(ê₁, ê₃'') = 55.0°
    Interactive Null-Space Explorer (Coupled ϕ & ψ):
    At Gimbal Lock, Axis 1 (ê₁) and Axis 3 (ê₃'') become collinear (ϕ + ψ = 70.00°). Drag the slider below or click Spin Null-Space: the outer and inner gimbal rings rotate continuously in 3D while the center object and matrix R stay 100% stationary!

    4. Solving for Euler Angles from R (Dual Solutions via atan2)

    Every non-singular 3D orientation R ∈ SO(3) is represented by two distinct Euler angle triplets. Clicking Swap Sliders to Alternate Solution Triplet flips the gimbal rings to the second solution while keeping the 3D object and matrix R identical.
